newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES leads Russian shares up on GDR launch.
newsitem.headline: UES leads Russian shares up on GDR launch.

text.p: Russian market bellwether UES shares skyrocketed by about 20 percent in early trade on Monday on news of a GDR launch, lifting leading shares, traders said, though some said UES could not maintain momentum.

At 0930 GMT UES ordinaries had risen to $0.3150, off a morning high of $0.3410, from $0.2798 on Thursday, the previous day of trade. UES ordinaries turnover was about $36.9 million, more than the entire market traded on Thursday.
An overhang of Western fund orders from Friday also spurred morning activity, traders said.
The Bank of New York said a global depositary receipt programme for trade outside the U.S. was live on Monday. The rumour had begun moving the market earlier.
"Everyone is buying UES," said Trinfiko senior trader Grigory Pinsky.
Pinsky said UES was bound to correct later in the day.
"Any share that rises more than 20 percent during a day must have a correction," he said.
Brunswick Director Martin Diggle, speaking mid-morning while UES was at about 31 cents, said the market looked strong for the day and the week, barring problems on international markets.
Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkhikvadze said Surgutneftegaz, Norilsk Nickel and Rostelekom were the quickest to follow the UES lead.
"UES is acting like a locomotive and other shares are like carriages," Chkhikvadze said. "The market is strong, bullish and there is support."
Surgutneftegaz rose to $0.875 from $0.829, Rostelekom edged up to $3.93 from $3.85 and Norilsk Nickel was $5.87 after $5.60.
Pinsky said other shares would not rise as high as UES.
"I think other shares may rise, too, but by five percent at the most," he said.
